 KA TIE HALL, individually;
 NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN;
 META PLATFORMS, INC.;
 and JOHN/JANE DOES 1- 6,

                 Defendants.

                                                ORDER


         This matter is before the Court on Plaintiffs Motion for an Order Directing Completion of

  the Rule 26(f) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan (ECF _). The Court has

  considered the Motion, the memorandum, the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine with exhibits,

  and any response and reply.

         It is hereby ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED as follows.

          1.     Participants. Plaintiff and counsel of record for Defendants National Center for

  Missing & Exploited Children, Katie Hall, and Meta Platforms, Inc. shall participate in and

  complete the conference required by Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f).

         2.      Format. The conference shall proceed by substantive written exchange on each

  subject identified in Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(2)- (3), unless the Court directs otherwise.

          3.      Completion date. The conference shall be completed no later than 14 days after

  entry of this Order.

         4.       Report date. The parties shall file the written discovery-plan report within 14 days

  after completing the conference and no later than 18 days after entry of this Order, unless the Court

  expressly sets a different reporting deadline.

          5.      Report contents. The report shall state the parties' agreed proposals and each

  party's separately attributed position on each subject in Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(±)(3), including any

  proposed sequencing or phasing of discovery, any requested postponement of discovery and the

  grounds for it, and any proposed protective or scheduling terms. The report shall not portray any

  party's disagreement or silence as assent. A party that declines to address a subject shall be

  identified as having declined.

          6.      Incomplete participation. If the conference remains incomplete, the parties shall

  file a joint status report by the reporting deadline. A party unable to obtain a joint report shall file

  its own report by that deadline. Each report shall identify the participation, exchanges, and

  remaining obstacle. A status report does not constitute completion of the conference, extend the

  completion deadline, or excuse further participation.

          7.      Relationship to other orders. The deadlines in this Order govern unless another

  order of the Court expressly sets different dates for the parties' Rule 26(f) conference or report. If

  the Court sets a scheduling conference under Fed. R. Civ. P. 16(b) by order on Plaintiffs Motion

  for Entry of a Scheduling Order (ECF _) or otherwise, any coordinated conference and reporting

  dates shall be calculated from the date of that scheduling conference as actually set and shall be

  achievable after entry of the order setting them. The pendency of Plaintiffs Motion for Entry of a

  Scheduling Order does not postpone compliance with this Order. The preparatory intervals under

  Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(l) and 26(f)(4) and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(l) are shortened to the extent

  necessary to meet the dates set by this Order or by any such order.

         8.      Existing matters. Nothing in this Order adjudicates any pending motion, defense,

  or objection, including the pending motions to dismiss (ECF 10, 21, 45) and the pending objections

  and applications concerning ECF 84 and ECF 96, and nothing in this Order modifies any existing

  order except as expressly provided. Participation in the conference does not waive any defense,

  including any asserted immunity, and does not require any party's agreement with any other

  party's proposal.

         It is SO ORDERED.
